evidence_fragments.content:
ABSTRACT
Pneumonia changes across respiration, inflammation, and organ function, while the
measurements that describe it arrive at different times and are often incomplete. We
introduce PULMOWORLD, a world model for longitudinal pneumonia dynamics
that connects asynchronous state estimation, recursive simulation, and evidence-
constrained planning. History-aware filtering separates state propagation from
observation-driven correction, so a measurement updates the shared belief only
when it is observed. That belief supports recursive forecasts of clinical values
and modality representations, and summaries of future prognosis. Cap-MBRL
searches imagined continuations inside an authorized action set and replaces a
frozen fallback only when a candidate meets the risk budget and a predicted-cost
margin. On the pneumonia cohort MASS, recursive forecasts are competitive
with task-trained sequence models, and simulated future states retain prognostic
information. Trained separately on public MIMIC-IV-CXR chest radiographs and
clinical trajectories, this model improves prognostic discrimination over latest-
value fusion in development and is competitive on long-horizon error on the locked
pneumonia panel. In five known-mechanism MASS-Syn environments, Cap-MBRL
lowers selection regret relative to direct fallback execution.

Materials and access.We will release evaluation code, preprocessing specifications, synthetic
mechanisms, and aggregate results. MIMIC-IV and MIMIC-CXR must be obtained under the
PhysioNet data-use agreement (Johnson et al., 2023; 2019); we do not redistribute these records.
MASS was used with permission after personal identifying information was removed. Its patient-level
clinical, CT, and BALF records are not part of the public release. Any qualified request for controlled
access remains subject to institutional permission and the applicable data-use conditions.
Evaluation separation.The locked MASS and MIMIC tests were evaluated after the respective
protocols were fixed. Test labels were excluded from training, model selection, calibration, and
threshold fitting. Development ablations and history-enabled prognosis use separate validation popu-
lations, as specified in Section C.5. Uncertainty estimates resample patients for clinical comparisons;
MASS-Syn policy comparisons instead summarize independent simulated environments. These
sources of uncertainty should not be interpreted interchangeably.
Scope of reproducibility.The appendix specifies cohort construction, model dimensions, loss
functions, training schedules, comparator interfaces, and case-selection criteria. Clinical forecasting,
representation prediction, and synthetic policy selection remain distinct evaluations: Cap-MBRL is
tested on known-mechanism MASS-Syn, while real-cohort action analyses assess care-conditioned
forecasts and authorization.

capability_assessments.rationale: MASS Clinical19 implements and evaluates recursive state forecasting; action residual explicitly disabled.
MIMIC parent is separately dimensioned state-only forecasting, not the action adapter.
Functional same-origin alternative-action prediction comparisons and factual held-out evaluation support L3; identification gate closed, no clinical causal efficacy inferred.
Simulator-only learned world drives optimized policy with closed-loop decision-quality evaluation. No patient care or real causal transfer.

legacy_cells.C: Tang, Cheng, Zhang, Xinyu, Chen, Jiawei, Zhang, Minghui, Wei, Shaocong, Li, Wei, et al.
legacy_cells.S: Can an evolving latent patient belief from incomplete longitudinal evidence forecast future clinical values and modality representations, and can imagined authorized actions improve selection in a known-mechanism simulator?
legacy_cells.T: Pneumonia patients in the MASS institutional cohort and MIMIC-IV-CXR; the locked forecasts include 40 MASS patients and 300 MIMIC pneumonia patients.

legacy_cells.AK: Frozen Qwen2.5-VL-7B CT feature encoder; imaging representations are reduced to 64 dimensions by train-only PCA (the frozen CXR representation is also prepared this way).
legacy_cells.AM: Masked observation-driven belief correction followed by gated cross-compartment messages in a shared patient belief; missing modalities supply no correction.
legacy_cells.AN: Boolean masks distinguish missing values from observed zeros; missing measurements have zero correction gain; future availability is decoded separately.

legacy_cells.AT: Propagate the prior over elapsed time, then apply a masked innovation correction from available evidence; uncertainty and evidence freshness are tracked separately.
legacy_cells.AZ: Structured blocks correspond to respiratory, renal, inflammatory, hemodynamic, global-severity, lung-imaging, and lung-metabolic states.
legacy_cells.BD: MIMIC fluid and vasopressor dose levels/templates (fluid in mL/kg; vasopressor norepinephrine-equivalent rate in µg/kg/min) over six-hour intervals; MASS action context includes medication/organ-support classes and interval attributes.
legacy_cells.BF: Candidate actions are restricted to a fixed authorized set after predictive, action-shuffling, support/overlap, and identification checks; replacements must satisfy a risk budget and beat fallback predicted cost by a fixed margin.
legacy_cells.BL: MIMIC measurements are assigned to six-hour bins while elapsed event-time gaps are retained; MASS uses irregular, recorded day-level event timing. Forecasts are evaluated through H1–H4.
legacy_cells.BN: A sparse graph connects physiological state blocks (including global-severity links); a bounded elapsed-time gain and evidence-reliability gates modulate transitions/messages.
legacy_cells.BS: Recursive clinical-value forecasts, imaging (CXR/CT) and BALF latent-representation forecasts, and future-availability predictions; imaging outputs are representations, not generated pixels.
legacy_cells.BT: Observation decoder heads for clinical values, modality representations, and availability; frozen outcome probes evaluate mortality prognostic information in predicted states.
legacy_cells.BU: MASS-Syn reward is negative latent severity; decision-time cost combines discounted predicted severity and weighted risk, with risk-budget and fallback-improvement constraints.
legacy_cells.BV: World-model loss combines masked Gaussian negative log-likelihood for reconstruction/recursive future values, availability binary cross-entropy, and applicable auxiliary alignment/consistency terms; MASS-Syn transition ensemble uses one-step latent-state MSE; actor objective uses imagined-return advantages, KL to behavior, and risk-budget penalty.

limitations: All 49 physical pages directly read, including references and appendices; all 17 figures and 21 tables inspected via rendered page contacts. This is one reviewer, not independent human adjudication.

Clinical19 uses seven internal blocks from three modalities. Action residual disabled there. MIMIC action adapter and synthetic policy are separate model configurations; do not import L4 or causal claims into real forecast models.
Native timestamp coarsening, true variable availability and last-measurement age are not fully audited; strict-online eligible MASS transitions are 285 versus 2569 retrospective.
Source-reconstruction nominal 95 percent coverage of 90.0 percent is not trajectory calibration; patient-bootstrap error intervals are sampling uncertainty, not predictive intervals.
Real action adapter identification gate is closed and authorized real control set empty. Functional L3 comparison does not establish causal treatment effects or clinical utility.
Known-mechanism synthetic L4 has no prospective patient/control evidence. Complete generator coefficients and numerical gate tolerances are not fully disclosed.
Fixed fallback can violate candidate risk budget; hard authorization does not certify all simulated action safety.
Private cohort counts/subcohort descriptions and some DirectVLM aggregate endpoint/change relationships require clarification. No correction invented.
Clinical favorable main-text examples are outcome-selected; complete CXR gallery selected by coverage. Observed CXR/CT examples are not generated image forecasts; tokens/latents are forecast.

Release is planned, not verified available code/weights. No actual runtime hardware latency, external shared-checkpoint validation, prospective clinical benefit or new named IRB identifier established.
